Me: I'll sleep early tonight.
Also me at 3 AM: watching how bricks are made.
Opening the fridge every 10 minutes like new food is going to spawn.
Me cleaning my room: finds an old notebook, reads it for 2 hours.
"I'm on my way" — me, still in bed, with zero intention of moving.

My phone at 15%: panic.
My phone at 15% when I'm at home: "she'll be fine."
Typing a long message, deleting it, sending "ok."
Saying "you too" when the waiter says "enjoy your meal."
When someone says "we need to talk" and your brain plays every mistake since 2009.
The 5-minute nap that turned into a 3-hour coma.
Rehearsing a phone call 10 times and still saying "you too" when they say "bye."

Me: I'll only watch one episode.
The sun: rising.
Checking the time, forgetting immediately, checking again.
"Let's hang out sometime." Both of us knowing it will never happen.
Pretending to text when you're alone in public.
Me after 1 productive hour: I deserve a 4-hour break.
Hearing your own voice on a recording and wanting to change your identity.
When the teacher says "find a partner" and your best friend is absent.
Waking up 2 minutes before the alarm and feeling robbed.

Me: I need to save money.
Also me: adds 14 things to cart "just to see."
Saying "I'm fine" so convincingly that even I believed it.
Me at a party: looking for the host's pet to hang out with.
That moment you walk into a room and forget why you came in.

Making plans: so excited.
The day of the plans: please cancel.
When someone says "no offence" you know offence is coming.
The confidence of someone singing in the car until they stop at a red light.
Me reading the same sentence 5 times because my brain left the chat.
Holding the door for someone who's too far away, so now they have to run.
"Five more minutes" is the biggest lie I tell every morning.
When your mom says "we have food at home" and the food at home is ingredients.
Group projects: 1 person does everything, 3 people "add finishing touches."
Laughing at a joke you didn't hear because everyone else laughed.

Me: I'm going to be productive today.
Also me: reorganises apps on my phone.
The internal panic when someone says your name in a conversation you weren't part of.
Rewatching the same show for the 7th time instead of trying a new one.
When the Wi-Fi drops for 2 seconds and your whole life pauses.
Having 47 tabs open and no idea which one is playing music.
"I'll do it tomorrow." Tomorrow: "I'll do it tomorrow."
When you wave back at someone who was waving at the person behind you.

My bank account: 0.
Me: buys a ₹300 coffee to feel better.
Me in the shower: winning arguments from 2017.
When the food delivery app says "your order is 2 minutes away" for 20 minutes.
That moment when you pull a push door in front of everyone.

Me: I don't care what people think.
Also me: re-reads my own message 10 times after sending.
Accidentally liking a 3-year-old photo while stalking.
When you finally get comfortable in bed and realise you left the light on.
Me trying to look busy when the boss walks by.
Studying the night before the exam like it's a movie montage.
The fake "I'm busy" face when someone you don't want to talk to walks by.
Leaving a party without saying bye to anyone.

Me: I'll cook something healthy.
Also me: orders biryani.
Typing "lol" with a completely straight face.
When someone asks "what's your favourite movie?" and you forget every movie ever made.
That one friend who's always "5 minutes away" for an hour.

Me buying a new notebook: this is the year I'll be organised.
The notebook: 3 pages used.
When you hear your phone vibrate but it was just your imagination.
"We should do this more often" — everyone, never again.
Pretending to understand someone after asking them to repeat themselves 3 times.
That feeling when you find money in an old jacket.

Me: wakes up tired.
Also me at 11 PM: fully awake, planning my entire future.
Telling yourself you'll only check one notification.
Me opening my laptop to work: checks YouTube "for 5 minutes."
When you finally decide what to watch and your food is already finished.
That moment you realise you've been talking on mute.

Me: I'll go to the gym tomorrow.
Tomorrow me: there's always next week.
When you laugh so hard no sound comes out and you just clap like a seal.
Reading the terms and conditions: never happened. Not once.
When someone says "guess what" and you have zero guesses.
Me pretending to read the menu even though I'm ordering the same thing as always.
Waiting for someone to reply like it's a life-or-death situation.
Me trying to act normal after tripping in public.
When you want to sleep but your brain wants to replay every awkward moment.

Me: I don't need anything from this shop.
Also me: leaves with 3 bags.
That feeling when you sit down and realise the remote is across the room.
When a song you haven't heard in years comes on and you know every word.
Me when someone takes the last slice of pizza: smiles, says nothing, never forgets.
Me the night before the exam: learning the entire syllabus from a 10-minute YouTube video.

The teacher: "This won't be in the exam."
The exam: entirely that.
Writing "I'll start studying at 7" and then waiting for 8 because 7:04 isn't a round number.
Opening the textbook, reading one line, rewarding myself with a 2-hour break.
When the professor says "any questions?" and everyone stares at the floor.
The silence after the teacher asks "who wants to present first?"
Group study: 10 minutes of studying, 3 hours of gossip.

Me: I'll make notes this semester.
My notes: a doodle and the date.
The confidence after writing an answer that's 3 pages long and 0% correct.
When the question paper looks like it's from a different subject.
Me checking the results with one eye closed.
When the class topper says "I didn't study at all" and gets 98.
The last bench: where legends are made and syllabus is ignored.
Sitting in the front row by accident and regretting every life choice.
When the teacher looks at the class and you avoid eye contact like your life depends on it.
Attendance at 74%: the most dangerous number in college.
Calculating exactly how many classes I can bunk and still get attendance.
Me in the exam hall: writing everything I know, plus some things I don't.

Exams in 2 days: panic.
Exams tomorrow: acceptance.
When you study one chapter and every question comes from the other chapters.
That one friend who says "bro, it's an easy paper" and then you fail together.
The joy of the teacher being absent.
"Open book exam" sounds easy until you realise you don't know which page anything is on.
Me after the exam: never discussing answers with anyone. Ever.
The library: where I go to sleep in a quieter place.
When the assignment is due at midnight and it's 11:52.
Changing the font size to 12.5 so the assignment looks longer.
Adding "in conclusion" to a paragraph that concluded nothing.
Copying a friend's homework and changing a few words so it looks original.
The "viva" where the examiner asks one question and you forget your own name.
When your crush sits next to you in the exam hall and your concentration leaves the building.
Highlighting the entire page because everything looks important.
When you finally understand a topic the day after the exam.
"I'll just rest my eyes for 5 minutes" — me, waking up during the next class.
Pressing the spacebar to see if my laptop still works, every 5 minutes, during online class.
When the teacher says "We'll finish early today" and then teaches until the last second.
Hostel life: Maggi for breakfast, lunch and existential crises.
When someone asks for extra sheets in the exam and you've barely filled one side.
Opening the result page and closing it immediately.
Being proud of passing an exam I was sure I'd fail.
The best study music is the one that makes me not study.
Me waiting for the bell like it's the last train home.
Turning in an assignment I'm not proud of, but at least it's turned in.
When the WhatsApp class group suddenly becomes active at 2 AM before the exam.
Asking "is this important?" about every single topic.
The PowerPoint with 47 slides that I made at 4 AM.
When the professor says "I'll take a surprise test" and the surprise is my heart rate.
Spending more time decorating my notes than actually reading them.
Me trying to read my own handwriting from last week.
Five people in a group project, and one of them is "busy" for the entire semester.
"Let's study together" — two people, one phone, zero studying.
The moment you realise your exam is tomorrow, not next week.
When someone says "I'll explain it in 5 minutes" and explains it in 2 hours.
Writing the date at the top of the page like it's going to help.
Reading "explain with examples" and having no examples.
When the invigilator walks past and you suddenly forget how to write.
Pretending to take notes during a boring lecture while texting.
Getting the answer right but losing marks for "not showing the steps."
When you write the perfect answer for the wrong question.
That "it's over" feeling when the last exam ends.

Me in first year: "I'll be so disciplined."
Me in final year: "Is it today?"
The joy of "no class today" texts.
When you realise you're the oldest person in the hostel corridor now.
Packing your whole life into one bag before semester break.
The deep friendship you form with the person who shares their notes.
"I'm going to start fresh next semester." Classic.
Eating instant noodles and calling it a balanced diet because it has vegetables in the packet.

The relief when the teacher says "the exam will be easy."

Thinking about switching careers during every exam season.
Every single time: "I should have started earlier."
That one subject you never understood but somehow passed.
Me calculating how much I need in the final to pass: 147 out of 100.
When the mock exam is harder than the actual exam, and you're still scared.
Graduation photos: smiling, but secretly wondering what comes next.

Me: puts phone down.
Me, 4 seconds later: picks phone up.
Opening Instagram, closing it, and opening it again 2 seconds later like something changed.

Screen time report: 9 hours.
Me: there must be a mistake.
Watching a 30-second reel 6 times because I wasn't paying attention.
"Just one more reel" — me, 2 hours ago.
Leaving someone on read by accident and then feeling too awkward to reply.
Seeing "typing..." and then nothing. The suspense is unbearable.
Sending a message and immediately noticing the typo.
Posting a story and checking who viewed it every 3 minutes.
The panic when you accidentally video call someone.
When you hit "like" on someone's old photo while stalking and want to move to another country.
Saving 400 reels I'll "watch later." I will never watch them later.
Taking a photo of a beautiful sunset that looks nothing like the real thing.
Typing "hahaha" with the exact number of "ha"s to show I found it moderately funny.
Charging my phone to 100% and then sitting next to the charger anyway.
When your phone shows 1% and you start using it like a bomb disposal expert.
Spending 20 minutes choosing a caption for a photo nobody will read.
Muting a group chat and checking it anyway.
When someone sends a voice note longer than 2 minutes: I'll listen later. (I won't.)
The silent judgement of sending a sticker instead of a real reply.
When someone replies "k" and your whole day is ruined.
Getting 1 notification and it's an app reminding me it exists.
When you open the app to do one thing and forget what it was.
That moment you check the time on your phone and immediately forget it.
Clearing notifications without reading a single one.

Recording a voice note 5 times because you sounded weird.

Typing a message, deleting it, typing it again, deleting it, sending a meme instead.
Waiting for someone to post a story so you can reply to it and start a conversation.
The feeling when your phone vibrates in your pocket but it didn't.

Me: reads a text.

When you have 3,000 unread emails and you've accepted it as a lifestyle.
Sending a meme to the group chat and nobody reacts. Embarrassing.
Opening YouTube to watch one video and ending up on a documentary about deep-sea fish.
Spending more time choosing what to watch than actually watching it.

Liking a post and immediately unliking it, hoping they didn't notice. They noticed.

Hiding your report card like it's a crime scene.

"Is your homework done?" — the answer is always "almost."

Being told to "study hard" and "enjoy your youth" in the same sentence.

The steel tumbler that's been in the family longer than you.

Getting a call from home and immediately thinking: what did I do?

Being the family's tech support since the age of 12.

Weddings where you know 3 people out of 800.
When aunties ask "When's your turn?" at every wedding.
Visiting relatives and being forced to eat more than humanly possible.

Pretending to be asleep so you don't have to carry the shopping bags.

That one relative who always asks for your Wi-Fi password the moment they arrive.

Pretending to type when my manager walks by.

Buying groceries for healthy meals and ordering takeaway anyway.
When you get your first salary and realise how much your parents spent on you.
Opening the electricity bill like it's a horror movie.
When you're asked "where do you see yourself in 5 years?" and you can't plan tomorrow.
Working from home: 10 steps from bed to desk, still late.
Wearing a formal shirt with pyjamas on a video call.
Saying "you're on mute" at least 5 times every meeting.
Taking a "quick" lunch break that lasts 90 minutes.

Sunday evenings: the existential dread before Monday.

Being too tired to sleep. Adulthood is weird.

Me a week later: what budget?
Paying ₹99 a month for a subscription I forgot I had for 6 months.
When someone asks "what do you do for fun?" and you realise you don't remember.
Ordering food and then waiting by the door like a puppy.
Doing laundry and then living out of the basket for a week.
Adding things I've already done to my to-do list so I can tick them off.
When you finally clean your room and can't find anything.

Me: buying plants.

Cooking for one and somehow making food for five.
Every adult conversation eventually turns to rent or back pain.
When your back hurts for no reason at all.
Getting excited about a new kitchen sponge. Adulthood.
Setting 5 alarms and snoozing every single one.
When the weekend goes by in a blink but Monday lasts a year.
Calling in sick and then feeling guilty all day.
"I'll start saving next month" — every month.
That feeling when a refund finally comes through.
When the delivery guy calls and you run like your life depends on it.
Pretending to understand the IT person's explanation.
When you finally reply to an email you've been avoiding for a week.
Me buying a planner to get my life together. The planner: blank since January.
Being proud of yourself for drinking water today.
The constant battle between "I want to go out" and "I want to sleep."
Me looking at holiday packages I absolutely can't afford.
When you finally have money but no time, or time but no money.
Working overtime and getting paid in "thanks, you're a star."
The "quick 5-minute task" that takes the whole afternoon.
When you get a raise and inflation gets one too.

Being an adult means getting excited when plans get cancelled.
That moment you realise your parents were right about everything.
Remembering an important task at 2 AM and then forgetting it by morning.
Spending ₹2,000 on a night out and then debating whether a ₹50 delivery fee is worth it.
When you're "fine" but you've had four coffees.
Stretching before getting out of bed like a 90-year-old.
That feeling of putting on fresh clothes straight out of the laundry.
Arriving at work and immediately counting down to lunch.
Saying "no worries" while having many, many worries.
The silent celebration when the meeting ends 10 minutes early.
When the boss says "we're a family here." Red flag.
Doing your best work at 11 PM, an hour before the deadline.
Updating my LinkedIn like it's going to change my life.
Ordering a salad to feel healthy and adding extra cheese to feel happy.
Being exhausted from doing absolutely nothing all weekend.
When the auto-reply says "out of office" and you feel jealous.
Me checking my bank balance after a weekend: who did this?
Every adult has a drawer full of chargers for devices they no longer own.
Paying rent: the most expensive way to feel nothing.

Me: I'm full.
Also me: sees dessert. There's always room.
Saying "I'll eat healthy from tomorrow" while finishing the last samosa.
Ordering the same thing every time because trying something new is too risky.
When the food arrives and someone says "wait, let me take a photo first."
Eating dinner while watching something and forgetting to taste it.

That moment when you drop food and do a quick five-second rule calculation.
Opening a packet of chips and finding it 80% air.
When someone asks "can I have a bite?" and takes half.
Midnight snacks taste better than any proper meal.
Me after eating biryani: needs a 3-hour nap.
When you're hungry, everything looks delicious, including the menu photos.
Me waiting for the pizza: checks the delivery app 47 times.
Accidentally biting your tongue and feeling betrayed by your own body.
When you finally sit down to eat and someone calls you.
Eating maggi straight from the pan because fewer dishes.
Searching the fridge for something new, finding the same stuff, closing it.

That moment you realise you've finished the whole packet without noticing.

Me: I'll sleep at 11.

Waking up before the alarm and lying there pretending it hasn't happened.

Sleeping on the edge of the bed even though the whole bed is yours.
Flipping the pillow to the cold side: a small victory.

Lying in bed doing absolutely nothing for an hour and calling it "self-care."
Taking a power nap and waking up in a different dimension.

When the alarm goes off and you negotiate with yourself like a hostage situation.
Snooze button: my best friend and worst enemy.
Waking up with a song stuck in your head that you haven't heard in years.
When you finally get comfy and need to use the bathroom.

When the fan makes a clicking noise and now you can't sleep.
Pretending to be asleep so you don't have to get up and switch off the light.
Trying to find the perfect sleeping position for 45 minutes.
That feeling when someone switches on the light while you're sleeping.
When you stub your toe and question every life choice.
Hitting your elbow on the funny bone. It's never funny.
Walking into a spiderweb and doing a full martial arts routine.
When the earphones get tangled in your pocket in a knot only science can explain.
Losing the TV remote and finding it in the fridge.
Searching for your phone while it's in your hand.
Searching for your sunglasses while they're on your head.
Forgetting someone's name 3 seconds after they tell you.
When someone waves at you and you can't remember who they are.
Walking into a room and completely forgetting why.
When you leave the house and immediately wonder if you locked the door.
Going back home to check, and the door was locked.
When it starts raining the moment you step outside without an umbrella.
Carrying an umbrella all day and it doesn't rain.
When the traffic light turns red the second you reach it.
Taking the shortcut and getting stuck in worse traffic.
When the lift door closes just as you reach it.
Pressing the lift button multiple times as if it'll come faster.
When someone sits next to you on an empty bus.
Getting a seat in a crowded metro: luckiest person alive.
Standing in the wrong queue for 20 minutes.
When the queue next to yours moves faster. Always.
That awkward moment when you both move the same direction to let each other pass.

Waving back at someone who wasn't waving at you.
Laughing at your own joke before finishing it.

Me after a week of it: I'm melting.
Monsoon: beautiful from the window, chaotic on the road.
Winter mornings: 10 minutes of courage needed to leave the blanket.
Overthinking a text so long that it's too late to reply.
Practising my order in my head while waiting in line.

Laughing at something on my phone in public and immediately looking around.
When someone says "can I ask you something?" and my heart drops.
Replaying a 2-second awkward moment for 2 years.
Walking the wrong way and pretending to check my phone to turn around.

Saying "you too" when someone says "happy birthday."
Accidentally making eye contact through a window.
Introducing yourself with the wrong name because you're nervous.

Being the first to arrive at a party and wanting to disappear.
Clapping when the plane lands, alone.
Waving at someone across the street and realising it's a stranger.
Sending a message to the wrong group chat. Panic.

Pretending to get a call to escape a conversation.
When you laugh at your own mistake to make it less awkward, and it makes it more awkward.
Pretending you know the song everyone's singing.
Holding a door, they hold the next one, now we're stuck in a door-holding loop.

Accidentally reading a stranger's screen and getting invested.
Practising a conversation in the shower and winning every argument.

Saying "I'm almost there" while still finding your shoes.
